thread:
maria_cs: Hey team — Sherwood's security contact pinged us about embeddings retention in the DPA questionnaire. They want: 1) retention default for generated embeddings, 2) whether customers can request export/deletion of vectors, 3) whether embeddings are stored encrypted with KMS. Can we draft a short answer? cc @devon_sec @jules_pm

devon_sec: Short answer: we offer configurable retention; default is 30 days for transient workloads, but for customers using Dedicated/Private they can opt to keep vectors indefinitely with encryption and key control. Need specifics for Sherwood's questionnaire though.

sam_eng: +1. Tech details: embeddings persisted in object store, encrypted at rest with KMS-managed keys; access audited. For Hosted customers retention is configurable per-tenant via console or API. Example API snippet:
```
POST /v1/embeddings/retention
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "retention_days": 30,
  "persist": false
}
```
We also have an export endpoint that streams vectors as newline-delimited JSON with base64-encoded vectors.

jules_pm: Thanks. Sherwood asked if we can provide a certified deletion log for compliance — can Legal confirm whether our deletion audit meets DPA/SOC2 evidence requirements?

legal_bot: FYI: For SOC2 evidence we can provide deletion events from audit logs (timestamp, actor, object id). We'll need a signed attestation if they require formal proof. Ping @devon_sec for any KMS key ownership clarifications.

devon_sec: Confirming: Hosted = RW-managed KMS keys by default; Dedicated can use customer-managed keys. Deletion path: we mark vectors for deletion, then background job wipes objects and logs event. Retention TTL is enforced by lifecycle worker; we can surface deletion request status in the console.

maria_cs: Can someone draft a one-paragraph FAQ answer we can paste into the vendor form? Sherwood needs it by EOD.

sam_eng: Draft:
"Redwood stores embeddings encrypted at rest. For Hosted customers, vectors are retained for a tenant-configurable period (default 30 days) and can be exported or deleted on request. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers may elect customer-managed keys and long-term retention. Deletion operations generate audit records (timestamp, actor, object identifiers) that can be provided for compliance reviews."

jules_pm: That looks good — add that exports are newline-delimited JSON and include metadata fields. Also add contact for a formal attestation: security@redwood.ai

maria_cs: Perfect. I'll paste this into the DPA form and flag the attestation option. Thanks all :thumbsup:

onboarding_bot: Document uploaded: https://docs.redwood.ai/sherwood/dpa-answers (access: sherwood@redwood.ai)

maria_cs: @sherwood-customer-contact just fyi we've uploaded the DPA answers and included the export/delete flow. If they ask for deeper logs, we'll route to security for attestation.
